articles.title: General Anesthesia vs Monitored Anesthesia Care With Local Anesthetic Infiltration (MAC-VL) for Ankle Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation: Impact on Recovery Metrics and Safety.
articles.authors: Kauffman TJ, Rangarajan R, Liss S, Burton A, Shi G, Kraus J
articles.population: Adults undergoing outpatient open reduction and internal fixation of ankle fractures
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: time to discharge from end of surgery to hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes: tourniquet time, operative time, anesthesia time, time in operating room, recovery room length of stay, conversion from MAC to GA, nausea and vomiting, hospital admissions, and emergency department visits
articles.take_home: Patients who had ankle fracture surgery under monitored anesthesia care with local anaesthetic infiltration (MAC-VL) went home about 55 minutes faster than those who had general anaesthesia, and also spent less time in the operating room. There was no significant difference in nausea, vomiting, admissions, or emergency department visits between the two groups.

articles.title: To Walk or Not? A Prospective, Randomised Controlled Trial to Evaluate the Effect of Weightbearing on Patient Outcomes Following First Metatarsophalangeal Joint Fusion.
articles.authors: Purdie SD, Glazebrook HM, Dissanayake R, Burgesson BN, Morash JG, Glazebrook MA
articles.population: Patients undergoing first metatarsophalangeal joint fusion for hallux rigidus or severe hallux valgus with osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 68 patients (33 immediate weightbearing as tolerated, 35 non-weightbearing)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: visual analogue scale pain scores and Foot and Ankle Ability Measure functional scores at 12 months. Secondary outcomes: non-union, complications including infection and wound issues, and patient satisfaction.
articles.take_home: Both immediate weightbearing and traditional non-weightbearing after first metatarsophalangeal joint fusion resulted in similar pain relief, function, and satisfaction at 12 months. Immediate weightbearing is safe and may allow patients greater mobility and independence during recovery.

articles.title: Evolving Management Strategies for Osteochondral Lesions of the Talus: A Contemporary Treatment Algorithm.
articles.authors: Rubin J, Tham A, Gauthier P, Murawski CD, Ferkel RD, Kennedy JG
articles.population: Patients with osteochondral lesions of the talus
articles.outcomes: Pain relief, functional improvements, cartilage repair, and durability of repair tissue across different surgical approaches
articles.take_home: There are multiple surgical options for treating talus cartilage injuries, chosen based on lesion size and type, ranging from preserving the original cartilage in fresh injuries to newer techniques using cell-based approaches or transplanted cartilage for larger lesions. Salvage procedures like joint fusion are reserved for extensive damage or failed prior surgery.

articles.title: Temporary screw epiphysiodesis for correction of ankle valgus in children with multiple hereditary exostoses : a case-control study.
articles.authors: Schmitz SI, Broja M, Andresen A, Doerell A, Saegebrecht L, Rupprecht M, et al.
articles.population: Children with multiple hereditary exostoses (MHE) and idiopathic ankle valgus
articles.sample_size: 37 MHE patients (68 ankles) and 35 control patients (56 ankles)
articles.outcomes: Correction of ankle valgus measured by lateral distal tibia angle; correction rate per month; duration of treatment; complications
articles.take_home: Temporary screw epiphysiodesis effectively corrected ankle valgus in children with MHE, achieving similar overall correction to children without MHE, but the correction happened more slowly and required longer treatment time. Treatment should be started earlier in MHE patients to achieve good results.

articles.title: From Sprain to End-Stage Osteoarthritis: Why Earlier Intervention in Ankle Cartilage Damage Deserves More Attention.
articles.authors: Hollander JJ, Dahmen J, Murawski CD, Gianakos AL, Takao M, Nakasa T, et al.
articles.population: Patients with ankle cartilage damage ranging from osteochondral lesions to end-stage osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Long-term outcomes of traumatic articular injuries and potential targets for early therapeutic interventions
articles.take_home: Ankle osteoarthritis causes significant burden similar to major chronic diseases and often follows ankle injuries. Early recognition and treatment of ankle cartilage damage may offer the best chance of improving long-term outcomes, but evidence for early interventions remains limited.

articles.title: Comparison of clinical and radiological outcomes of total ankle arthroplasty in two subtypes of varus ankle osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Jeong BO, Kim JH, Kim MS, Lee JH, Kyung MG
articles.population: Patients with varus ankle osteoarthritis undergoing total ankle arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Pain (visual analogue scale), AOFAS hindfoot scores, talar centre migration, hindfoot alignment angle
articles.take_home: Both types of varus ankle osteoarthritis improved with ankle replacement surgery, but translation-type osteoarthritis achieved better pain relief and maintained better alignment correction than rotation-type. Rotation-type osteoarthritis showed worsening alignment over time after surgery.

articles.title: Reverse and Frugal Innovations in Orthopaedics: Potential Applications in High-Resource Settings.
articles.population: Orthopaedic patients in high-income and low- to middle-income countries
articles.outcomes: Cost-effectiveness, access to care, safety, clinical outcomes of reverse innovations adapted to high-resource settings
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic solutions developed in low-resource settings, such as the Ilizarov fixator and Jaipur Foot prosthesis, can be adapted for use in wealthy countries to improve value and access to care. High-income countries should use pilot programmes and quality improvement methods when introducing these innovations.

articles.title: Does flexor hallucis longus groove morphology have an effect on flexor hallucis longus tendon pathologies?
articles.authors: Yesilli ME, Tokgoz MA, Baymurat AC, Ergisi Y, Ataoglu MB, Kanatli U
articles.population: Patients who underwent posterior ankle arthroscopy
articles.outcomes: Relationship between flexor hallucis longus groove shape and tendon degeneration
articles.take_home: The shape of the groove that holds the flexor hallucis longus tendon affects how likely the tendon is to become damaged. Deeper, narrower grooves were linked to more tendon damage, whilst wider and shallower grooves seemed to protect the tendon.

articles.title: Climbing is associated with tissue-specific mechanical adaptations of the plantar fascia and achilles tendon.
articles.authors: Burzynski M, Jurecka A, Walocha J, Rutowicz B, Groszyk A, Kwolek K, et al.
articles.outcomes: Oscillation frequency, dynamic stiffness, logarithmic decrement, mechanical stress relaxation time, and creep of foot and lower leg soft tissues; Foot Posture Index scores
articles.take_home: Climbers showed specific changes in their plantar fascia and Achilles tendon, including increased stiffness and faster recovery properties, suggesting that climbing causes localised adaptations to these tissues. These changes were not associated with differences in overall foot posture between climbers and non-climbers.

articles.title: Preoperative clinical and imaging factors associated with arthroscopically confirmed occult syndesmotic instability in patients undergoing surgery for osteochondral lesions of the talus.
articles.authors: Jia S, Fu K, Li Z, Hao C, Fang Z
articles.population: Patients with osteochondral lesions of the talus undergoing ankle arthroscopy
articles.outcomes: Preoperative clinical and imaging factors associated with arthroscopically confirmed occult syndesmotic instability
articles.take_home: About one in five patients with talus cartilage damage had hidden ankle syndesmotic instability found during surgery. Higher BMI (above 25.6 kg/m²), the presence of bone spurs, and thickening of Bassett's ligament were associated with this instability, though the findings need further research to confirm.

articles.title: The impact of changing Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification on early functional outcomes after primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Zaidi F, Goplen CM, Akbarshahi M, MacDessi SJ, Petterwood J, McEwen P, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Scores at baseline, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year; radiological measures including hip-knee-ankle angle and joint line obliquity
articles.take_home: Patients whose knee alignment changed significantly (across two classification types) after surgery had slower functional improvement in the first 6 months compared with those whose alignment stayed similar. Changes in thighbone angle of more than 4 degrees from the original position appeared to have a greater negative effect on recovery than equivalent shinbone changes.
